source_snapshot.procedure: Create one unused user ID with `user set name`, `user set password`, `user enable`, parameterized `user priv`, literal `channel setaccess 1 ... privilege=4`, literal `sol payload enable 1`, then check the user list.
source_snapshot.criteria: The new account is added successfully and displayed correctly.
source_snapshot.script: Internal `useraccount_check-add-set` path; exact revision and behavior are unavailable in this repository.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL supplies only name/password/enable and a generic list. It omits the source privilege, channel-access and SOL writes, hard-codes cipher suite 17, exposes both management and new-account passwords in command/process text, and does not define authoritative cleanup.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly adds disposable-slot discovery, protected secrets, per-channel baseline, access/SOL readback, bounded authentication and recovery, but incorrectly makes the source's literal SOL operation optional and leaves the placeholder-versus-literal source profile undecided.

old_problem: The prior review left Engineering Decision Pending because the first privilege command used `<Privilege level>` and `<Channel number>` while the next two source commands fixed channel 1, administrator privilege 4 and SOL enablement. It also treated SOL as optional and described cleanup as delete/disable even though standard IPMI disable does not erase an account or prove restoration of an unreadable prior password.
disposition_reason: The literal downstream source commands constrain the earlier placeholders for original-source conformance: instantiate `<Channel number>` as 1 and `<Privilege level>` as 4, keep link authentication and IPMI messaging on, and enable SOL payload for the same slot on channel 1. This preserves every source operation and eliminates the apparent conflict without guessing an OEM payload. Project identity, channel-1 applicability, dedicated scratch slot, protected secrets and an accepted tombstone cleanup state are runtime prerequisites. A different channel or privilege is a documented Project override and cannot be reported as passing the original profile.
decision_basis: XLSX row 940, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 941 were directly read; the next identity was verified as Functionality row 941 / variant 117f0bd41b469e7c.

The source explicitly follows the parameterized privilege line with `channel setaccess 1 ... privilege=4` and `sol payload enable 1`; binding the earlier placeholders to those literals yields one coherent source-conformance profile and retains all six writes.

Pinned upstream ipmitool source defines `user priv <id> <level> [channel]`, maps level 4 to Administrator, prompts twice when `user set password <id>` omits the password argument, and treats omitted user-list/privilege channels as the current channel. Explicit channel 1 is therefore required for this profile.

The upstream manual defines `channel setaccess <channel> <userid>` with independent callin/ipmi/link/privilege fields and SOL payload enable/status operations. A successful name write or user-list row cannot prove channel access or SOL state.

ED-03/ED-13 and ED-33 through ED-38 allow a standard, parameterized command contract with Project bindings while prohibiting guessed OEM behavior, unsafe execution, coverage loss and an AI-owned DUT verdict.

test_case.test_name: Create, verify and safely retire one disposable IPMI channel-1 administrator account with SOL payload enabled
test_case.purpose: Verify the original IPMI path can create and enable one approved disposable account, assign administrator privilege and link/IPMI access on channel 1, enable that account's SOL payload on channel 1, display every resulting field correctly and return the dedicated slot to its approved non-usable cleanup state without affecting protected accounts.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity, pinned supported ipmitool version, protected RMCP+ management credential path and approved cipher policy
Vendor/Project proof that channel 1 is the intended session-capable management/SOL channel and that source privilege 4 means Administrator on this target
Dedicated disposable numeric user slot proven non-protected and unused across every relevant channel, plus independent recovery administrator access
Approved <=16-byte username, target-supported 16/20-byte password policy, protected interactive/secret-provider input and no-secret evidence rules
Approved source profile: user ID, channel 1, privilege 4, callin baseline, link=on, ipmi=on and mandatory SOL payload enablement

Approved bounded read-only login probe and deterministic cleanup profile: SOL disabled, user disabled, channel-1 access set to no-access/link-off/ipmi-off, name cleared where vendor-supported, and password rotated to an approved tombstone secret because password contents cannot be read back
Exact pinned internal script revision if it is proposed; otherwise use reviewed direct ipmitool operations only
test_case.test_command: SECURITY-SENSITIVE WRITE; execute only after point-of-action approval. Preserve logs and capture complete per-channel slot/access/SOL baseline from an independent recovery session. Prove the selected dedicated slot is not fixed, occupied, protected or used on another relevant channel. For the original-source conformance profile, bind `<Channel number>` to `1` and `<Privilege level>` to `4`. Run once, with immediate exit-status/audit/readback checkpoints and no automatic retry: `ipmitool ... user set name <ID> <approved-name>`; `ipmitool ... user set password <ID>` with protected double prompt and no password argument; `ipmitool ... user enable <ID>`; `ipmitool ... user priv <ID> 4 1`; `ipmitool ... channel setaccess 1 <ID> link=on privilege=4 ipmi=on`; `ipmitool ... sol payload enable 1 <ID>`. Do not use `-P` or hard-code cipher 17 unless approved. Verify with explicit `user list 1`, `channel getaccess 1 <ID>`, `sol payload status 1 <ID>`, complete other-relevant-channel comparison and one bounded read-only login probe under the new account. Then, from the independent recovery account, retire only the scratch slot using the approved reverse sequence and prove the cleanup profile. Do not run the internal script without pinned inspection.
test_case.expected_result: All six source operations succeed exactly once on the approved disposable slot. Channel-1 inventory shows the approved username, enabled state, Administrator privilege, link authentication on and IPMI messaging on; channel access independently reports privilege 4 and the selected flags; SOL payload status reports enabled for that user/channel; the bounded protected login performs only its approved read action. No unrelated account, channel, SOL entitlement, session or audit state changes. Cleanup disables SOL and the user, removes channel access, clears the name only when supported, installs the approved tombstone secret and returns the slot to the exact Project-approved non-usable state.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires target/tool identity, explicit approval, a verified dedicated slot and recovery path, all six source writes with channel=1/privilege=4, independent user/access/SOL readback, a protected bounded login, no unrelated change and complete approved cleanup. Omitting privilege/setaccess/SOL, treating SOL as optional, using another channel/privilege without a recorded override, exposing a secret, relying on exit code/list alone, using an occupied/protected slot, or failing cleanup is FAIL and stops. If channel 1/admin/SOL is unsupported or prohibited, the original profile is NOT APPLICABLE only with authoritative platform/security evidence; otherwise missing bindings are NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Require separate point-of-action approval for the exact slot, name, channel-1 Administrator access, SOL entitlement, bounded login and cleanup sequence; do not auto-retry any failed write.
Maintain an independent recovery administrator session and exclude fixed, root, owner and break-glass accounts; stop on any slot/channel identity ambiguity or recovery-access change.

Never place either management or new-account passwords in `-P`, arguments, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review records; use protected prompts/providers and redact identity evidence by policy.
Do not clear SEL, security or audit logs. Preserve pre/write/post/cleanup evidence and stop on secret exposure, excess privilege, unexpected session, wrong channel or unrelated-account delta.

Do not reinterpret privilege 4 as least privilege or make SOL optional: they are explicit source coverage. A lower role or different channel requires an approved override and is not an original-profile PASS.

Do not claim that `user disable` deletes the account. Cleanup must independently remove access/SOL, disable the slot and establish the approved blank-name/tombstone-secret state with vendor-supported commands.
expected_evidence: Approval, target/BMC/ipmitool identity, channel-1 capability proof, protected-account list, dedicated slot and redacted complete per-channel baseline
Per-operation status and audit correlation for name, protected password, enable, privilege-4/channel-1, channel access and SOL payload enable
Complete `user list 1`, `channel getaccess 1 <ID>` and `sol payload status 1 <ID>` evidence plus other-relevant-channel no-change comparison
Protected bounded login/read-only authorization result and proof that secrets never entered command text or collected evidence
Reverse cleanup evidence proving SOL off, access removed, user disabled, approved name/tombstone-secret state, unrelated-account continuity and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Stop further writes at the first failed or mismatched checkpoint. From the already-open independent recovery session, record the state, disable SOL payload for the scratch ID on channel 1, remove link/IPMI access and set no-access, disable the user, clear the username only through the vendor-supported standard path, rotate to the approved tombstone secret, and verify every relevant channel plus protected accounts. If the wrong/protected slot changed or recovery access is impaired, make no speculative repair; use the approved BMC security recovery procedure and escalate with preserved audit evidence.

source_conflict.reason: The later literal source commands are stricter constraints, not equally weighted alternatives: they bind the preceding placeholders to channel 1 and privilege 4 and require SOL enablement. A Project may approve a different consistent mapping only as a traceable override, never as a silent original-source interpretation.

blocked.reason: Standard command semantics, checkpoints and a safe confirmation-gated lifecycle are defined. Target channel applicability, account policy, slot and tombstone cleanup are finite Project configuration/readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Target BMC/ipmitool/cipher policy; channel-1 and privilege-4 applicability; disposable slot; protected username/password provider; recovery account; bounded login; audit/redaction; vendor-supported blank-name and tombstone-secret cleanup profile.

external_authorities.title: OpenBMC user-management architecture
external_authorities.application: Corroborates channel-scoped IPMI user-access architecture and the need to preserve channel-specific account policy.

project_authority: The Project/vendor package must prove that channel 1/admin/SOL is applicable, allocate the scratch slot and protected secrets, define accepted cleanup/tombstone state and own PASS/FAIL/N/A. It may authorize a fully traceable different channel/role profile, but that result is an override and not an original-profile PASS.
